steps.text: Soak cedar planks for at least 1 hour in warm water. Soak longer if you have time.
Stir soy sauce, vegetable oil, rice vinegar, sesame oil, green onions, ginger, and garlic together in a shallow dish.
Place salmon fillets in soy mixture and turn to coat. Cover and marinate for at least 15 minutes, or up to 1 hour refrigerated.
Preheat an outdoor grill for medium heat. Place planks on the grill grate. Heat planks until they start to smoke and crackle just a little.
Remove salmon from marinade and place on planks; discard marinade.
Close grill cover. Grill salmon until it flakes easily with a fork, about 20 minutes; salmon will continue to cook after you remove it from the grill.

raw_recipe.headline: Cedar Planked Salmon
raw_recipe.description: Cedar plank salmon is a delicious way to cook salmon for moist results with a delicious smoky flavor. This recipe uses a quick soy and ginger marinade.

review.reviewBody:
I just made this last night and it was absolutely fantastic! I didn't have green onions so I used minced red onion. My in-laws were so impressed they wanted to have a plank to take home! Costco has them for $8 for a package of 6. The package on the plank states that if it's not too charred you can use is again after cleaning with warm water and letting it air dry. Also, to save time, planks can be presoaked and frozen. I can't encourage you enough to try this incredible recipe!
Thank you for the post.

Making it tonight. We've made a ton of salmon this way.Our go to topping is from Portland Palate - an amazing citrus capers combo. Tonight I will sub Aminos for Soy. Otherwise going with the listed mix. We start grilling with the salmon on the plank, no preheat. Previously used planks heat up quickly so no preheat needed. Also I look to remove the plank at or just before 135dF on thickest salmon. Setting plank in shallow baking tray with enough water to kill the smoke. Scents the dining experience wonderfully. Cedar Plank salmon cooking is Stupid Simple Masterpiece method. Don't be afraid, be rewarded. Lowe's or HD has untreated fence boards. They work great. The thick the better, 5/8 is better than 1/2 when you can get it. A special board is overkill. Scrap and rinse to use again. Walk the plank to a delicious dinner!"....................So, I made it. We loved it. Highly recommend. It was helped along by some killer fresh Columbia River salmon. Also I scoped up the ginger, garlic and green onion bits out of the marinade and topped the salmon.

Wow! This was excellent, and I'm generally not a fan of salmon. I really want to be, though, and this recipe helped tremendously! I made the marinade as directed, but I used olive oil instead of vegetable. I baked it instead of grilling. I thickened the remaining marinade on the stove with a little cornstarch slurry, and brushed the finished salmon. My husband really liked this, too, so I'll definitely make it again! We'll try it on the grill next time.

I've been making this recipe for years. I've let it marinate for 1 to 2 hours. I also sprinkle a little sesame seeds on the salmon once on plank. I then take the marinade strain it and place into sauce pan. I add a quarter cup of water and bring to boil. Then add a cornstarch slurry to thicken. Makes a great sauce on side for salmon and rice and even a green vegetable. I've also used this marinade on chicken breast chunks. I then skewer and grill. I'm gonna try using it on shrimp as another suggested.

I've been baking my salmon and had gotten so bored with the taste. I found this recipe (already had cedar planks in cupboard). So I went to for it!! I had to substitute powdered ginger unfortunately (I usually have it fresh on hand or diced up frozen). Well, my husband raved (I loved it too), and said hands down it's the best salmon he's EVER had. Ever! That is huge (we're old ...LOL). I did one additional thing. I hated to toss the marinade away so drained it into a small sauce pan and boiled it lightly and used it over the salmon after serving. So incredibly great!!!

The family loved it. I forgot the vegetable oil so I think it was more intense. Used shallots instead of green onions, and was really generous with the ginger and garlic. Plus I cooked it skin on (I can be a sloppy recipe reader!). I'm trying it again tonight (sans veg oil and sans skin) to see if I can repeat the magic! Served with broccoli and sweet rice (which is sticky). Did it in the oven 425 for about 15 minutes (but I'm not sure - I just watched the fish and tried not to over cook).

Made this last night and it was outstanding! Soaked the boards for about 3 hours. I did indirect grilling, the board never caught fire. I made a couple of minor tweaks, I used olive instead of vegetable oil, and used low sodium soy sauce. The ingredients were spot on. It was very flavorful, but not too overwhelming. One more thing, I kept the grill at 350 degrees and it took longer than I expected to cook through. Next time I'm going to try keeping the heat at 400. Can't wait to make it again!

I used the marinade from this recipe but cooked in the oven at 375 degrees. Placed fillets in aluminum foil, covered with extra marinade from soaking, and sealed. Placed sealed salmon in the glass dish, and baked 35 minutes. While baking, the whole house smelled heavenly! The salmon turned out very moist. I served it with rice and sprinkled it with fresh mint. YUM! I look forward to making this again!

I doubled the recipe for 12 of us. Children and grandchildren ( 5 under the age of 8) raved about it and all wanted more (unusual for the little ones). I soaked the planks for 6 hours and oiled the top surface prior to putting the salmon on it as suggested in another review. The planks did not go on fire, the salmon cooked to perfection and I was able to easily wash the planks after dinner with hot water. This allows me to use them again. Will definitely keep this recipe and do it again.

This is now my all-time favorite fish recipe, regardless of the type of fish. I followed the ingredients exactly, and highly recommend the extra effort of fresh ginger and garlic over the dry stuff. The only thing I did differently was I baked it in the oven. I still used the cedar plank and soaked it, then I lined a cookie sheet with foil and placed the plank on a wire rack over the cookie sheet. Baked at 360F until fish was 145F inside and it came out moist, flaky, and tender.

Nice recipe! It was my first time using Cedar planks. It was very easy. Smiths carries a 2-pack of planks for about $7. I marinated the fish for an hour and cooked for 19 minutes at a temp from 400*-425*. The finished product was subtly flavored and more moist than any cooking method I've ever tried in the house. I would add a pinch of salt and pepper next time before grilling. The marinade didn't make the fish salty on its own. Looking forward to trying more cedar plank salmon recipes now. Thanks for the inspiration!

I leave the skin on for flavour and generously top with brown sugar most of which dissolves and runs off to pique the finish flavour. I buy red cedar fence boards ( untreated of course) way cheaper than the thin shakes that stores sell and by having a thicker board it takes longer for the heat to get through the fillet so you get a little more smoke in the fish.

Quick and easy to make and consistently moist, flaky, and flavorful salmon. I briefly toss the remaining marinade to precooked Thai rice noodles in a hot wok for an equally easy and delicious starch on the plate.
Loved the ease with which this went together…this was as good, if not better than a restaurant! Nice, delicate flavor with no mess to clean up
Did it pretty much as directed. 400deg for 25 minutes.

I made this tonight and I must say, it’s going into the rotation of quick and easy meals. It tastes like a lot more effort went into it. I didn’t want to waste the marinade so after the filets went in the plank, I cooked the marinade down in a saucepan. SOOO GOOD!
Marinade had great ingredients but they didn't transfer to an outstanding flavor for salmon. Cedar plank didn't add much either. Finished dish was fine, just not great.

I grilled it with skin side down, on the cedar plank and it came out terrific. I did this on a gas grill and cooked to an internal temp of 135-140F. The meat was tender and flaky and came off the skin without issue. Thanks for the recipe!
Excellent recipe. Well written! I used a zip lock freezer bag for marinating. I used reduced sodium soy sauce. Grilling on cedar planks is a great way to cook salmon.

Very tasty, and it was easy to accomplish. Wild caught Coho was available at our grocery store. For my grill, “medium” heat was close to 400°F, so the actual cooking time was just 12 minutes. Fortunately, my son was able to assist and temped the salmon at that point. It’s a repeat!
